reviews.review_title: They refuse to delete and remove my account.
reviews.review_text:
I recently made a purchase through Aliexpress, as I always do, but unfortunately this time the products arrived completely damaged and unusable due to poor packaging by the seller.

reviews.review_title: Item not as ordered
reviews.review_text:
I ordered a dress to be made from a company called Fatapaese. I said all along for the dress to be made out of crepe. I said this right from the beginning the dress was to be Crepe and beaded lace. 
I got imitation silk and plain lace.
Not once was imitation silk even mentioned. 
The first dress they lied to me about it saying it had been made and shipped. That was a lie. They admitted they should have told me the truth.
So I sent the specifications of the picture which always said crepe and beaded lace. 
There were no live videos and photos of the making of the dress.
They showed me a picture right at the end and I had no idea it was not crepe and beaded lace.
I have the whole transcript from beginning to end. I only ever mentioned crepe and beaded lace. The picture was shown and shipped at the same time. I said to them I only want the dress if it's in crepe and beaded lace. They led me to believe this was what I was getting. Not once did imitation silk get mentioned. 
It was only when I received the dress I knew the material was incorrect.
So I opened a dispute saying item not as ordered.
Ali Express did not care. Although I provided all the transcript that said a crepe dress and beaded lace they did not care and ruled in favour of the seller.
$277 it cost me for a dress I did not order in the material they made it in.
PayPal did not want to know either because they don't cover customised dresses. Although the item was not as described. 
Don't trust the sellers or Ali Express. They do as they please and there is no protection for the buyer. 
This was a dress for my daughter's wedding.
I had already had 2 other dresses made by another company that were the wrong size and they got away with that too. They were Charmant Wedding Stire Don't trust them. They can make inferior products and get away with it.i paid over $600 for nothing. I cannot wear any of the dresses because they were made incorrectly. Ali Express say this is ok.
Pay more and go local.

reviews.review_title: Poor after-sales support when a defective product is delivered
reviews.review_text:
I purchased a hair brush through AliExpress and unfortunately received a defective product.

I understand that manufacturing defects can happen with any company. My disappointment is not with the defect itself, but with how AliExpress handles these situations.

The only solutions offered were:

accept a small partial refund and keep a defective product; or
package the item myself, travel to a post office, and complete the entire return process in order to receive a full refund.

The issue is not the product's value (around US$10). The issue is the principle.

As a good-faith customer, I fulfilled my part of the contract: I selected the product, paid for it, and waited for delivery. The defective product was entirely the seller's responsibility. Nevertheless, AliExpress transferred the burden of solving the problem to me, requiring me to spend my own time and effort on a return process that I never agreed to when I made the purchase.

When everything goes well, delivery is made to my home. When something goes wrong because of the supplier, I'm expected to become part of their reverse logistics operation.

I find this policy unfair and contrary to what good customer service should look like. I expected AliExpress to take responsibility for resolving a problem it caused, instead of transferring the inconvenience to the customer.

I hope the company reviews this policy and adopts a more customer-friendly approach in cases where defective products are delivered.

reviews.review_title: WORST refund process
reviews.review_text: WORST refund process.  I bought 2 identical pairs of shoes, just in different sizes.  Neither fit and had to be returned.  Even though both pairs arrived to me TOGETHER, AliExpress made me return them separately (even though I began the return process at the same time).  I chatted with AA to express my concerns that separating the two pairs of shoes might cause return delivery issues, especially since AA had me return one pair via Fed Ex and the other pair via USPS.  My concerns turned out to be valid.  One return pair of shoes was received by AA and they refunded me.  However, AA claimed they did not receive the other pair.  Like I said, they should not have been returned separately since I received them together originally.  I had ample documentation from USPS stating that the items was delivered to the Linwood, NJ post office AND that the item was actually picked up by an individual.  As directed by AA, I even had my USPS receipt stamped with the USPS official seal and signed by USPS staff.  I had at least 3 disputes over this and at least 3 trips to USPS.  I sent AA reasonable proof that the item was in fact returned to the post office AND picked up by an individual.  It was not good enough for AA to refund me a crummy $11.82!  The would NOT have happened if AA permitted me to return both pairs together, just like they were delivered to me originally.  I have had to return many things over the years to Temu, Shein, Walmart, Amazon, Etsy, and Ebay and I have never dealt with such impossible requests.  Although the AliExpress chat teams have been professional and empathetic, I felt like they "yessssed" me to death, but did nothing.  I deactivated my AliExpress account and will NEVER do business with AA again.

reviews.review_title: A month of broken promises over a return shipping refund
reviews.review_text:
I’ve been going in circles with AliExpress support for over a month now, and I’m writing this because at this point nothing else has worked.

The short version: I returned an item and paid for the return shipping myself, on the express understanding that it would be refunded. That wasn’t me assuming anything. Before the package even reached the seller, support told me in chat to keep the proof of payment because the shipping would be refunded once the return was complete. The return form in the app said the same. And the shipping cost was almost as much as the item itself, so if anyone had told me it was on me, I’d never have sent it back. It wouldn’t have been worth it.

Then it just became a wall.

July 7, they confirmed in writing: the shipping fee would be refunded based on the receipt. July 8, I sent the receipt, and there’s a logged reply on their side proving it. July 9, they closed the case saying they never got a valid response. That’s simply not true, and their own system shows it.

After that their escalation team offered a coupon as the refund format, and confirmed it twice, once on July 14. Issued within 1 to 5 business days if I replied within 24 hours. I replied on July 15, inside their own deadline. The coupon never showed up in my account. Not once. What I got instead was another email telling me no refund was possible at all.

So they promised, ignored my reply, closed the case for “silence,” then offered a coupon themselves, I accepted, and now it’s suddenly impossible. Every step of that is documented in their own emails.

What actually gets me isn’t even the money. It’s the lying. Different agents, same recycled lines, and a written promise from their own senior team that they’re now pretending never happened. A month of that.

If you’re reading this while deciding whether to buy from them: keep every screenshot, don’t trust a verbal or chat promise, and know that “we’ll refund it” can quietly turn into “policy says no” the moment the item’s back with the seller.

I still just want the coupon they already promised me in writing. That’s all.
